content: Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillin, or to cephalosporin antibiotics. Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as corn (in products containing dextrose), which can trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Penicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Some formulations of this medication may contain sodium or potassium, which should be considered if you have conditions requiring dietary restrictions of these elements. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary, as determined by your healthcare provider. It is important to note that this drug can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as specific urine glucose tests, potentially leading to false test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney function, complete blood count, and potassium/sodium levels, may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. It is crucial to take each dose as prescribed. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It is also employed to prevent bacterial endocarditis (infection of the heart) in patients with certain heart conditions undergoing surgery. It belongs to the class of natural penicillin antibiotics. Depending on the specific product, this medication is administered via injection into a vein or muscle. Use it exactly as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by a healthcare professional on its preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. If you are also using aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin), administer them separately from this medication. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Common side effects may include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. When used to treat syphilis or other spirochetal infections (e.g., Lyme disease), this medication may cause a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction. This condition typically occurs 1 to 2 hours after receiving the medication and can last up to 24 hours. Rarely, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
